prediction.likelyOutcome: Navient should recover its conceded $503,822.72 cooling tower claim largely intact, with BPG's $817,845 counterclaim substantially reduced — the transformer claim likely time-barred, the rooftop claim likely capped near repair cost rather than replacement cost, and the heat pump claim likely trimmed from the age-based $434,500 theory down toward the narrower operability-based figure. Net result is a probable six-figure recovery in Navient's favor, before any fee award, though a worse-case scenario where the court credits BPG's experts broadly could leave Navient owing a net setoff instead.

outcome.description: The Superior Court entered post-trial judgment for Navient in $503,822.72 (the conceded cooling-tower reimbursement) less $79,650 awarded to BPG on its counterclaim ($71,250 to repair 25 non-operational heat pumps and $8,400 to repair two rooftop air units), a net principal of $424,172.72 plus prejudgment interest from March 17, 2020; BPG's transformer and elevator claims failed. Navient was held the prevailing party entitled to its attorneys' fees and expenses under lease section 28(q) (amount not stated). This is the trial-level decision; no appeal is reflected in the source.
